purpose: Full built-out checklist applied to every estate job row (live, archived, proposed); also serves as the intake checklist for future jobs (recommendation — see intake_rule; not enforced by disposition logic). A job is fully built out only when every item is PASS. UNKNOWN is never PASS, FAIL, or zero. This pass rate is NOT D85 admission: D85 requires rig-determinism-85 score (four ratios >= 0.85) plus a bound checklist artifact; d85_classification on a row is a body-class annotation, NOT_EVALUATED for D85 admission here.
intake_rule: Governance recommendation — NOT enforced by the collector's disposition logic: before a future job enters KEEP, all identity/evidence/routing items should PASS, criteria coverage should reach >= 0.85, and no one-way (irreversible) effect should lack failure-mode + done-test evidence; otherwise treat as INVESTIGATE. Enforcement in disposition_for() is a named follow-up, not current behavior.
validation_semantics: Per-item PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN is CHECKLIST VALIDATION over evidence the authorities expose; it is NOT a test of job execution. Observed execution results live only in C08 (last run) and C09 (last result), and rows whose authority exposes neither are untestable-from-evidence, not failed. Prefect is unreachable, Kestra exposes no execution results, and most launchd plists carry no last-execution timestamp in this collection. C11/C12 and C19-C23 evaluate over facts attached by the collector's contract/classification passes, never over absence.
lattice_note: Lattice coordinates come from rig_lattice.route_intent (pure keyword rules, no model) at neutral 0.5/0.5/0.5 BMS priors; per-row calibration is a named human decision, never model-filled.

items.q: Does the row carry a stable source:id?
Is the owning scheduler authority one of the six registered authorities?
items.fix_hint: assign the row to a registered authority

items.q: Are lifecycle facts recorded as separate installed/enabled/loaded flags (launchd) or an explicit lifecycle state (other)?
Is the trigger kind parsed from the authority record?
Is the executable target known (command, workflow type, prompt body path, or workdir)?
Is a named owner evidenced?
items.fix_hint: name the owner for <id> in the worksheet

items.q: Is a named consumer evidenced (proposal consumer or goal mechanism)?
items.fix_hint: name the consumer for <id> in the worksheet

items.q: Is a last run evidenced? (judged only for authorities that expose run history; other sources are UNKNOWN = untestable from evidence, not failed)
items.fix_hint: run <id> once with an evidenced timestamp

items.q: Is a last result evidenced? (judged only for authorities that expose a result field — hermes lastRun status, Temporal workflow status; Orca exposes lastRunAt but no result, launchd/Kestra results not collected; UNKNOWN = untestable from evidence, not failed)
Does the job map to a goal (revenue, fitness, James, learning, telos) through a named mechanism?
items.fix_hint: name the goal mechanism for <id> in the worksheet

items.q: Is the failure mode documented?
Is a measurable done-test recorded?
Was duplicate analysis run against normalized command/target/schedule (group evaluated, not label similarity)?
Was the framework-precedence decision applied with a named reason?
Is a lattice coordinate assigned (Lx-Dy-Bz, deterministic keyword router)?
Is a BMS mode + confidence recorded for the job?
Does 20-criterion evidence coverage reach 85% (unknown never scored)?
Is a decided disposition recorded (KEEP/MIGRATE/RETIRE/PROPOSED; INVESTIGATE = undecided)?
Does exactly one live scheduler (off-state verified) hold the job?
Is the owner + rollback migration binding recorded?
Does the owner scheduler show renewal evidence (schedule/keepalive/catch-up plus one green run)?
Is there a verified run within max(7d, contract.freshness) with an output reference?
Is the trigger-owner selection evidenced (or default_used via Kestra)?
